anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: The 12 pre-existing tick symbol-days are permanently exploratory - never sealed, never `historical_oos`, never relabeled. (critical)
anti_goal_violations.evidence: OPEN - a NARROW HOLE in the safeguard this iteration installed, not a present breach. Audit B2, confirmed by the evaluator: _tick_dataset_session_dates (walkforward.py:995) drops DatasetStore.list()'s _errors channel, so a dataset whose file is unreadable or whose checksum is broken at seed time is silently omitted from the window list - and because a NON-EMPTY seed flips the has_any_exposure_entries guard, that window can never be seeded later, leaving a future spec over it classifiable as historical_oos. Cannot fire today: I read the real store's integrity_errors and it is empty, and the fully-empty case self-heals (zero windows appends zero rows, so the guard stays false). Same defect SHAPE as the iteration-3 finding where a corrupt playbook record was silently skipped rather than reported. Fix: report-or-refuse on the _errors channel instead of dropping it; the playbook seed one line above needs the same treatment.

anti_goal_violations.anti_goal: No exploratory read of a sealed shard / the 12 pre-existing tick symbol-days are permanently exploratory. (critical) - read forward: a SEALED shard must never be marked exposed either.
anti_goal_violations.evidence: OPEN and LATENT UNTIL J-06 - recorded now as a binding J-06 prerequisite. Audit B1: the new seed marks every dataset DatasetStore.list() returns as exposed, with no sealed filter, and the once-per-registry has_any_exposure_entries guard makes the first seed permanent. Safe today because datasets.py carries no sealed concept at all and the real store's 18 datasets contain no sealed member (both checked). The moment J-06's vault lands sealed shards in .data/datasets, a first seed on a fresh registry could mark a sealed window exposed and it could never be historical_oos again - the inverse of the rail this fix protects. No field exists to filter on until the vault ships, so inventing one now would breach T-1. Fix belongs in J-06: seed by an explicitly recorded legacy symbol-day identity (or a source_kind / vault check), never by 'whatever is registered now'.
